title: A dependency change that would close a loop is refused
The refusal leaves an ephemeral notice naming the tasks in the loop; it is not a persistent condition
The two notice lifetimes are persistent and ephemeral, replacing the earlier "one-off"
A persistent notice lasts while its condition holds, an ephemeral one stays until it is dismissed, and dismissal of a persistent notice hides it until its condition clears
Tool shape is flat, one tool per operation; names are snake case, prefixed by the noun they act on (task_create, session_start, notice_dismiss)
Each tool has a strict parameter schema of its own; the product's job is a well-named, strictly described inventory
Every identifier parameter accepts the bare integer or the display form, TSK-42 or PRJ-7
There is no prefix matching and no fuzzy target, consistent with identifiers being integers
A display form naming the wrong record kind is an error rather than a lookup into the other kind
Every failure returns a stable machine-readable code, a human message, and the offending entity or field
The known codes include confirmation_unavailable, confirmation_denied, confirmation_timeout, confirmation_attempts_exhausted, session_not_started, active_timer_conflict, estimate_required, ...
A call that needs a human's approval does not execute; it records a pending operation with a two-digit code, a five-minute expiry, and an attempt count, and returns the operation id
The code reaches the human through the strongest channel available: an ephemeral notice on an attached interactive surface, else an OS notification, else a private log file, else a free stream
The human gives the code to the agent, which calls the confirmation operation with the operation id and the code, at which point the stored intent runs; the agent keeps the operation id
Three failed attempts kill the pending operation, and re-requesting creates a new one with a new code
Trust assumptions per channel decide the order: a window, the tray, and an OS notification are agent-proof; a private log file only if the agent has no filesystem access; ...
With no channel at all, confirmation_unavailable still applies, as the specification says
Every read of a changing thing takes an optional cursor and returns the complete current state plus the changes since that cursor, grouped per entity, each group headed as the history
One general change feed returns everything since a cursor regardless of entity, grouped the same way, and its header states plainly that it must not be used to reconstruct state
Every response hands back a fresh cursor for the next call
The cursor is opaque to the caller: it is the change log's sequence position, dressed so a caller cannot do arithmetic on it, not a wall-clock time
Every change records the surface it came from, one of command line, desktop, tray, and agent, and whether a human or an agent drove it
There is no user identity field: a single-user local tool cannot honestly claim one
The per-type OS flags, configurable levels, quiet hours, and one-delivery-per-condition from decisions-forecast-warnings stand
This pass adds the delivery ladder, which the confirmation code shares
The notice list is always the authoritative place, so an OS copy is never the only trace of a condition
